summary: Osier Ridge's 1961 R-6 cab on the Clearwater National Forest has been continuously staffed since its first 1921 structure, with known lookouts dating to 1931.

access.note: Drive-up site; staffed seasonally, so it may be occupied by a Forest Service volunteer.

events.note: Log cabin with a 30-foot pole platform tower, the first lookout at the site.
Mark E. Lawrence staffed a partial season.
Pole tower (40-55 ft per different sources) with L-4 cab built.
A newlywed couple ran the lookout out of Kelly Creek Ranger Station, continuing into 1959.
Current 15x15 R-6 flat-top cab with catwalk built on a 40-41 ft timber tower.
Added to the National Historic Lookout Register, April 6, 2009.
Volunteer Nate Raff staffed the tower in late summer; Idaho Fire Lookouts' authors subsequently joined the volunteer staff roster.

evidence.supports: 1921 first structure and 1961 current tower, still active
evidence.quote: In 1921 the Clearwater National Forest built a pole platform tower and a ground cabin at Osier Ridge Lookout, which was replaced with a 40' pole tower with L-4 cab in 1938. This 15'x15' R-6 flat top cab with catwalk on a 40' timber tower was built in 1961 and is still active.

evidence.supports: Osier Ridge history timeline and staffed status
evidence.quote:
Osier Ridge was first a log cabin and a 30' pole platform in 1921.
1938 – 55' pole L-4 was built.
1961 – 41' TT R-6 Flat tower was built.
This tower is staffed during the fire season.
pole tower with L-4 cab in 1938, the present 41' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, built in 1961, is staffed every summer.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says 40 feet; Idaho Fire Lookouts says 55 feet. Both describe the same 1938 L-4 pole tower; likely a measurement or transcription discrepancy between sources.
NHLR says 40 feet; Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com say 41 feet. Treated as the same structure given matching design (R-6) and year.

notes_for_editor: Height figures for both the 1938 and 1961 structures differ slightly between NHLR and Idaho Fire Lookouts; recorded as a range in the story rather than resolved, since no source explains the discrepancy. Story's 1921 sentence reworded so it no longer implies the pole platform sat on top of the cabin — sources describe them as two separate structures built together.
